subject: URGENT: Cypress Health — request for geo-failover authorization and exec bridge
messages:
From: Sara Ng <sara.ng@cypresshealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production spike — sustained 5xx / token latency (AZ us-west2-3)

Grace — we are seeing a sustained spike of 5xx errors and token-level latency ~3x normal across our HV endpoints since ~08:30 PT. Traffic is concentrated to us-west2 AZ-3 per our telemetry (attached CSV). Users are experiencing timeouts and retries which is amplifying load.

Key impact: 15% of inference requests returning 500s, median token latency jumped from 60ms to 180ms, customer-facing payment verification flows are timing out. Team has attached sample logs and a screenshot of the dashboard.

We need this escalated to take one of the following ASAP:
- Immediate geo-failover to us-east2 (customer preference) OR
- Emergency routing diversion + temporary traffic throttling with a clear customer comms plan.

Please advise a remediation path and whether Redwood can open an exec bridge. We are on standby.

Thanks,
Sara
Director of Platform Ops, Cypress Health

Subject: RE: Fwd: Production spike — sustained 5xx / token latency (AZ us-west2-3)

Grace / team — quick technical summary from the account-side:
- Telemetry indicates concentrated QPS increase to us-west2 AZ-3; backend pool in the zone is saturated (queue depth rising, token queue timeouts).
- Immediate mitigation path (recommended):
  1) Initiate geo-failover to us-east2 using policy "regional-diversion-customer-consent". This will re-route new sessions to the east region.
  2) Spin up reserved capacity (dedicated burst) in us-east2 (we have capacity pool available for Cypress; boot time estimated 8–12 minutes).
  3) Apply prefix/KV cache warming for high-frequency endpoints to reduce cold-start amplification.
  4) Apply transient 10% throttling to non-critical routes (analytics, background inference) to protect payment flows.
- Estimated customer-facing recovery window: 12–20 minutes after failover trigger, risk of increased latency for long-running requests during KV warming.

Need exec sign-off for: opening the exec bridge and approving a one-hour courtesy credit (suggested one hour of token credit) so we can proceed without delay on comms.

Attachments: runbook-geo-failover-v2.pdf (high level checklist).

Monica
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sara Ng <sara.ng@cypresshealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-27T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Production spike — sustained 5xx / token latency (AZ us-west2-3)

Adding technical detail from runtime:
- Root cause signal: KV cache saturation + request amplification from retries. We also see a model-variant that allocates larger KV memory per session at this tenant's config — this makes it more sensitive to queueing under burst.
- Actions I can run immediately if we get sign-off:
  * Trigger routing policy switch: `POST /admin/routing/redirect {account: "cypress-health", to_region: "us-east2"}` (requires ops token).
  * Bring up east capacity: kick off dedicated-burst job `reserve-capacity --pool us-east2 --units 8` (est 8–12m).
  * Temporarily pin to "low-kv-variant-v1" to reduce per-session memory footprint (risk: slight quality degradation on edge cases).
- Rollback plan: re-enable original routing policy and drain east pool; revert variant pin.

I'll stand by to execute once Markus gives the green light on the exec bridge + credit. If we do the routing switch first, we should push a short notification to Cypress ops to avoid simultaneous client-side retries.

Rishi
Principal Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
